title: changelog: generate enterprise-style LTS release notes (grouped sections + risk + issue links)
author: Connor O'Brien
description:
Context: Enterprise/Dedicated/Private customers asked for LTS patch notes that are slower-change and operationally useful (SUP-3988, PM-812). Our current changelog output is optimized for internal dev velocity (chronological, includes noisy refactors, limited context) and doesn’t encode risk or provide consistent issue traceability.

This PR updates the changelog generator to produce an LTS-oriented format suitable for publishing as Confluence release notes and attaching to audit evidence. The output is grouped into stable sections, each entry includes a risk level, and we surface issue links (Linear/Jira) deterministically.

What this changes:
- Adds an LTS output mode: `--channel=lts` and `--lts-branch=runtime-1.20-lts`.
- Generates grouped sections (in this order): Security, Correctness, Reliability/Stability, Performance, Ops/Release Engineering, Docs.
- Adds per-item risk tagging (LOW/MED/HIGH) using a simple rule set + optional PR label overrides (e.g. `backport-risk-high`, `backport-risk-medium`).
- Adds issue link extraction + normalization:
  - Linear keys: ENG-/PM-/DES- parsed from PR title/body + optional `Linked-Linear:` trailer.
  - Jira keys: SUP-/INT- parsed from PR title/body + optional `Linked-Jira:` trailer.
  - Output includes a consistent “Traceability” line for each entry (e.g. ENG-4826, SUP-3950).
- Reduces noise by default in LTS mode:
  - Excludes PRs labeled `internal-refactor`, `deps`, `ci-only` unless explicitly forced via `--include-noise`.
  - Collapses multi-commit PRs to a single bullet, preferring PR title, with optional “Notable sub-changes” for Security.
- Adds a “Known issues & exclusions” footer stub (populated later by release notes author; included here to keep structure consistent across patches).

Why it matters:
- Enterprise ops teams want to quickly answer: what changed, how risky is it, do we need to do anything, and what tickets does it map to.
- For LTS we need predictable formatting for audit evidence and customer comms.

Usage:
- Standard (unchanged): `./tools/changelog/gen --from v1.20.0 --to v1.20.1`
- LTS: `./tools/changelog/gen --channel=lts --from runtime-1.20-lts.0 --to runtime-1.20-lts.1 --output release_notes.md`

Example output snippet (LTS mode):
- Correctness
  - [LOW] Fix scheduler token accounting under bursty streaming workloads (PR #8427) (Traceability: ENG-4826, SUP-3950)
- Performance
  - [MED] Reduce KV cache fragmentation for long-context decode (PR #8433) (Traceability: ENG-4827)

Testing:
- Added unit tests for grouping, issue parsing, and risk inference.
- Added golden-file snapshots for LTS output to prevent formatting regressions.

Notes/Follow-ups:
- This intentionally does not publish to Confluence; it only produces markdown that the release checklist can consume (ENG-4828).
- Risk inference is conservative; if we can’t infer risk, we default to MED in LTS mode to force human review before publish.

Checklist:
- [x] Backward compatible default output
- [x] Deterministic ordering
- [x] Golden tests
- [x] Docs updated (`tools/changelog/README`)
- [x] Works on release/* branches

tests: add golden snapshots for LTS output
docs: document LTS changelog usage + flags

conversation:
Elliot Price (review): The section ordering matches the release notes template, good. Can we avoid showing empty sections? Connor O'Brien (author): In LTS mode I’m intentionally emitting empty headers (with “(none)” suppressed) so release notes have stable anchors for ops runbooks. Added `--omit-empty-sections` for ad-hoc runs; default remains stable anchors.

Sahana Iyer (review): Risk inference defaulting to MED might create noise for doc writers. Can we default LOW? Connor O'Brien (author): For enterprise patches we’d rather over-review than under-review; MED forces explicit downgrade in the PR label when safe. Added explicit label `backport-risk-low` and documented it.

Noah Patel (review): Please ensure we don’t accidentally include internal refactors in LTS output. Connor O'Brien (author): Updated filters: in LTS mode we exclude `internal-refactor`, `deps`, `ci-only` unless `--include-noise`. Added test that a deps-only PR is omitted.

Dev Patel (review): Can we guarantee SUP- tickets show up when present? Connor O'Brien (author): Yes, parser now scans title/body and also recognizes `Linked-Jira:` trailers; added unit coverage.

Final approvals: Elliot Price ✅, Sahana Iyer ✅, Noah Patel ✅. Merged after green CI.
release_notes: LTS changelog generator now supports enterprise-style grouped output with risk levels and Linear/Jira traceability links.
Default (non-LTS) changelog output remains backward compatible.
